heuristics: Random-mapping behaviour of the class walk with s = 2^20 adding-walk branches (Teske 2001; Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe 2011 penalty sqrt(1 + 1/s)), covered by a 5% step margin

Jump indices and conjugation choices of distinct classes are independent and uniform; the fruitless-cycle counts (lengths 3 to 2048) rest on this; the index and distinguished-test bits come from a charged mix of the key, treated as a random function

Fruitless cycles of length at most 64 are detected at a fixed period of 64 steps and escaped by squaring the state at the least-key member of the cycle; longer cycles are bounded only by the trail self-collision bound (2^-42.6 trapped trails over the run, each costing at most 2^84 steps)
The success bound uses N_eff = N' (1 + 1/16) (1 + 2^-15): with T = 1.05 k + 2^104 productive visits, P = 1 - exp(-T^2/(2 N_eff)) = 0.401, above the required 0.39 with a 1.019 margin in visits
limitations: Analytic cost; no full-size execution; toy-scale experiment only.
Memory is astronomical (2^53.7 bytes, distinguished-point rate 2^-80) and unscored.
Per-step instruction count is an estimate from blst's 383 instructions per Fp multiplication, charged with a margin.
